scope: Six official indicators covering El Segundo, the Los Angeles metropolitan area, California, U.S. retail coffee prices, and the global green-coffee market. This is a bounded source-backed teaching edition, not a local business census or shop revenue database.

facts.title: U.S. retail coffee prices
facts.summary: The national coffee CPI-U category increased 6.1% over twelve months. Its August month-to-month change was −0.9% before seasonal adjustment.
facts.limitations: It is not a café menu-price index, wholesale bean quote, dollar price per pound, local demand measure or shop margin.

facts.title: Los Angeles food service price backdrop
facts.geography: Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim; Los Angeles and Orange counties
facts.summary: The area's food-away-from-home CPI-U increased 2.4% over twelve months and was unchanged from July to August.
facts.limitations: The metro index is broader than coffee, is not seasonally adjusted, and has a smaller sample than the national CPI. It does not measure an El Segundo café or compare price levels between cities.

facts.title: California general wage floor
facts.summary: California's general minimum wage is $16.90 per hour for employers outside a higher industry or local wage requirement.
facts.limitations: Some localities and industries have higher requirements. Do not apply this general floor to every café or chain; verify the workplace and applicable rules. The calculator’s $19,000 fixed budget is an invented teaching assumption, not a statutory wage or reported shop payroll.

facts.title: El Segundo resident context
facts.summary: Census estimates 16,379 city residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020–2024 median household income is $150,737 in 2024 dollars.
facts.limitations: City residents are not the population of the 25-mile atlas. Household income is not individual purchasing power; neither figure counts café customers, commuters, airport visitors or daytime workers. Five-year income estimates are historical averages.

facts.title: Global supply outlook
facts.summary: USDA forecasts 2026/27 world coffee production at 189.7 million bags and consumption at 179.7 million bags; each bag is 60 kilograms.
facts.limitations: Forecasts can change. Marketing-year calendars vary by country. Production minus consumption is not a shop profit, delivered inventory forecast or complete stocks/trade accounting. Do not splice these figures with ICO coffee-year balances without explaining their different periods and methods.

facts.title: Global green-coffee price signal
facts.summary: ICO's composite green-coffee indicator averaged 287.29 US cents per pound in August, compared with 287.26 in July.
facts.limitations: The composite is not the invoice price of a specialty lot or roasted bag. Differentials, quality, contracts, currency, freight, yield loss and timing affect a roaster's actual cost.

methodology.collection: Read official BLS, Census, California DIR, USDA FAS and ICO pages or reports directly. Search results alone were not treated as evidence. Merchant-specific cases must be grounded in the separate café/roaster source research.
methodology.date_handling: Observation date is October 3, 2026. Release dates, effective dates and statistical periods are independent fields. Unknown publication days remain null.
methodology.geography: Resident figures describe city limits; LA CPI describes a two-county metro area; state wage rules depend on workplace jurisdiction; national/global indicators do not resolve individual shops.
methodology.model_handling: All business-model numbers are hypothetical. Models deliberately omit actual merchant revenues and private financial data.
limitations: This is not an exhaustive census of cafés, roasters or market conditions.
No shop's stock, sales, revenue, employment or customer retention has been inferred.
Public assortment and opening-hour pages can become stale and require merchant rechecking.
Data from different agencies have different definitions and periods; forecasts cannot be compared as realized sales.
A sensitivity exercise illustrates a mechanism and cannot forecast a specific shop's outcome.
methodology.attribution: Use direct source links adjacent to each statistic. Paraphrase factual statements; no third-party artwork is included in this research file.
